text:
Anna: heads-up — we saw a sudden spike in svc->svc call failures in east-west, primarily from the GPU model-serving pool. lots of DNS retries and a flurry of `i/o timeout` lines in the node-local-dns logs.
Liam: how bad are we talking? p50/p95/p99? any correlation with autoscaler events?
Anna: p50 ~ steady, p95 up ~200ms, p99 jumps ~1.2s. errors are mostly `dial tcp: lookup svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout` and repeated CoreDNS SERVFAILs during the window. autoscaler did some scale-up but pods were stuck in Init waiting on sidecar DNS lookups.
Sophie: can you paste the node-local-dns logs (recent window) + a `kubectl get endpoints` for affected svc?
Anna: pasted below (trimmed):
```
Apr 11 15:28:03 node-23 node-local-dns[2211]: lookup timeout: "model-worker.default.svc.cluster.local" -> 10.0.0.10:53
Apr 11 15:28:03 node-23 node-local-dns[2211]: cache miss, forwarding to CoreDNS
Apr 11 15:28:03 coredns-0 coredns[134]: error serving request: read udp 10.0.0.10:37320->10.1.1.2:53: i/o timeout
Apr 11 15:28:04 node-23 node-local-dns[2211]: exceeding max inflight queries, dropping 12 requests
```
Anna: `kubectl get endpoints model-worker -n default` returned endpoints but some IPs were flapping due to kube-proxy conntrack drops.
James: tagging network oncall @james — could this be conntrack exhaustion / iptables sync backlog on nodes with heavy GPU pod density? we had similar symptoms before but not with this magnitude.
Maria: also saw MTU mismatch warnings on one node - `packet too big` on the RDMA-enabled NIC around the same time. likely some host-level MTU/ENI change during maintenance window?
Liam: interesting — so three hypotheses: (1) node-local-dns overwhelmed by insanely high fanout from model workers (prefix/KV cache cold fill), (2) conntrack table getting saturated causing replies to be dropped, (3) MTU/fragmentation hitting RDMA path and causing UDP DNS retries.
Sophie: quick checks to run: `ss -s` on nodes, `conntrack -L | wc -l` and compare to conntrack_max, `ip -s link` for MTU drops, and CoreDNS metrics `/metrics` for `request_duration_seconds_bucket`.
Anna: ran `conntrack -L | wc -l` on node-23 -> 65530, conntrack_max=65536. so we're at the ceiling.
Infra-bot: [metric alert] dns.request.errors (core-dns) spiked 6x between 15:27-15:35; link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/dns-spike/1851234567
Liam: that explains dropped replies. conntrack overflow will drop new flows and that shows up as timeouts in UDP-based DNS.
Maria: RDMA fabric also showed 10% retransmit increase; I suspect fragmentation because some pods use hostNetwork=false with huge overlay MTU while RDMA NIC expects smaller MTU.
Sophie: mitigations: immediate — increase conntrack_max (+20%), bump node-local-dns max-concurrent-requests, and temporarily reduce model-worker startup fanout (rate-limit init probes). medium — pin heavy-serving pods to nodes with dedicated NICs, tune MTU/overlay settings, enable eBPF conntrack offload if available. long — sharding CoreDNS/placing local CoreDNS per-AZ and see if we can move node-local cache to LRU with higher capacity.
Anna: trying quick patch: applying sysctl `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072` on affected nodes and scaling node-local-dns replicas from 1->3 on high-density pools.
Deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/conntrack-bump -> infra/gpu-pools; canary on node-23.
Liam: also opening a short incident doc so we track RCA and follow-ups. assigned to James + Maria for network & RDMA checks, Sophie for CoreDNS tuning, Anna for runtime mitigations.
James: will run `conntrack -F` on one node after we confirm safe to flush (low traffic window) and coordinate with schedulers.
Maria: I'll coordinate with cloud vendor on ENI/MTU drift logs.
Sophie: record of immediate action items in the doc: 1) conntrack_max bump and observe 2) node-local-dns replicas increase 3) rate-limit model-worker init fanout 4) schedule RDMA deep-dive.
Anna: thanks — will update when canary stabilizes or if spike recurs. :thumbsup:
